title: Cryptocurrency & Blockchain Privacy Hardening Checklist
metaDescription: Complete privacy checklist for crypto users. Secure your transactions, protect identity, and maintain anonymity with proven blockchain privacy techniques.
intro: Blockchain transparency can expose your financial activity to surveillance and tracking. This comprehensive checklist helps you implement essential privacy measures for cryptocurrency transactions, protect your identity, and maintain anonymity across different blockchain networks.

items.why: Standard wallets often leak metadata and don't implement privacy features, making transactions easily traceable by chain analysis.
items.howTo: Choose a wallet with manual coin control and Tor support: Wasabi or Electrum for Bitcoin, Cake Wallet or the official GUI for Monero. Avoid leaving balances with a custodial exchange.

items.task: Generate new addresses for each transaction
items.why: Address reuse links all your transactions together, creating a clear financial history that can be analyzed and tracked.
items.howTo: Enable automatic address generation in your wallet settings. Never share or reuse receiving addresses. Use HD wallets that create new addresses from a single seed phrase.

items.task: Use hardware wallets with privacy features
items.why: A hardware wallet keeps your private keys offline, so malware on the computer you sign from can't take your coins.
items.howTo: Use a hardware wallet with software that gives you coin control and Tor. Note that Trezor Suite dropped its CoinJoin feature on 1 June 2024 when the coordinator it used shut down, so don't pick a device for that.

items.why: Lost access to privacy wallets can force you to use less private recovery methods or lose funds entirely, compromising your privacy setup.
items.howTo: Write down seed phrases on metal backup plates, store in multiple secure locations. Test recovery process with small amounts. Never store digitally or in cloud services.

items.task: Separate wallets for different use cases
items.why: Using one wallet for all activities links your transactions together, reducing privacy and making it easier to build a complete financial profile.
items.howTo: Create separate wallets for: long-term storage, daily transactions, DeFi activities, and privacy mixing. Never mix funds between wallets without proper privacy measures.

items.why: Without coin control, wallets may automatically combine UTXOs from different sources, linking previously separate transactions and reducing privacy.
items.howTo: Enable manual UTXO selection in wallet settings. Avoid combining coins from different sources in single transactions. Use coin labeling to track UTXO origins.

items.task: Know what CoinJoin is before you use anything that calls itself a mixer
items.why: A self-custodial CoinJoin never takes your keys. A custodial mixer does, and FinCEN treats one as a money transmitter.
items.howTo: Prefer techniques where you keep your keys: coin control, new addresses, and privacy coins. Note that zkSNACKs shut down the CoinJoin coordinator behind Wasabi and Trezor Suite on 1 June 2024, so consumer options are thin.

items.why: Transactions sent immediately after mixing or at predictable intervals can be correlated, reducing the effectiveness of privacy measures.
items.howTo: Add random delays between mixed transactions (hours to days). Avoid round numbers and use varied transaction amounts. Don't follow predictable patterns.

items.why: Centralized exchanges require KYC verification and maintain detailed transaction records, linking your identity to all trading activity.
items.howTo: Trade on DEXs like Uniswap, SushiSwap, or Bisq. Use different wallets for DEX trading and connect through Tor or VPN. Avoid linking to centralized exchange accounts.

items.task: Convert to privacy coins for transfers
items.why: Transparent blockchains like Bitcoin and Ethereum expose all transaction details, making privacy difficult to maintain for transfers.
items.howTo: Convert to Monero or Zcash shielded for a transfer, then convert back if you need to. Check what the services at each end do with funds that passed through a privacy coin before you commit.

items.why: Any connection between your crypto addresses and real identity can compromise all related transactions, past and future.
items.howTo: Never use the same addresses for KYC exchanges and privacy transactions. Avoid posting addresses publicly or linking them to social media accounts.

items.task: Connect to crypto networks through Tor
items.why: Direct connections to blockchain networks expose your IP address, linking your real location and identity to your cryptocurrency activity.
items.howTo: Configure wallets to connect through Tor. Look up your own addresses through your own node or over Tor, because a block explorer can log which addresses you search from which IP address. Set up Tor routing for full nodes if running your own infrastructure.

items.task: Use VPN for additional connection privacy
items.why: ISPs and network monitors can track your crypto-related internet activity, potentially correlating with blockchain transactions and compromising privacy.
items.howTo: Connect to privacy-focused VPNs like Mullvad or IVPN before crypto activities. Choose VPNs that accept crypto payments and don't log activity. Where a wallet can connect through Tor, that alone hides your IP address; adding a VPN doesn't make Tor more anonymous.

items.why: Connecting to third-party nodes exposes your wallet addresses and transaction queries, allowing node operators to link addresses to your IP.
items.howTo: Set up Bitcoin Core, Monero daemon, or other full nodes locally. Connect wallets only to your own nodes. Use Tor for node connectivity to hide IP address.

items.why: Unsecured connections can expose crypto activity to local network monitoring, compromising transaction privacy and wallet security.
items.howTo: Use encrypted WiFi (WPA3), avoid public networks for crypto activities. Use cellular data or personal hotspot when necessary. Enable firewall and network monitoring.

items.why: DNS queries to crypto-related domains can reveal your interests and activities to ISPs and DNS providers, creating metadata trails.
items.howTo: Use privacy-focused DNS like Quad9 or Cloudflare. Configure DNS over HTTPS (DoH) or DNS over TLS (DoT). Use Tor Browser for crypto-related web browsing.

items.why: Sophisticated adversaries may use network analysis to correlate crypto activities with other online behavior, compromising privacy.
items.howTo: Vary connection patterns and timing. Use different networks and locations for crypto activities. Monitor network traffic for unexpected connections or data leaks.

items.why: KYC exchanges maintain permanent records linking your identity to all transactions, which can be subpoenaed or breached, exposing your crypto activity.
items.howTo: Peer-to-peer platforms such as Bisq and Hodl Hodl hold trades in escrow without taking custody. When you do use a verified exchange, withdraw to a wallet you control rather than leaving a balance.

items.task: Use different exchanges for different purposes
items.why: Using one exchange for all activities creates a comprehensive financial profile that can be easily analyzed and potentially shared with authorities.
items.howTo: Separate exchanges for: fiat on/off ramps, altcoin trading, and privacy coin purchases. Avoid linking accounts or using same verification documents across platforms.

items.why: Direct withdrawals from KYC exchanges to final destinations create clear audit trails linking your identity to specific addresses and recipients.
items.howTo: Withdraw to a wallet you control rather than straight to a final destination, and use coin control afterwards so that withdrawal isn't spent alongside an unrelated coin.

items.why: Data breaches at exchanges can expose not just transaction history but personal documents and information, creating identity theft risks.
items.howTo: Use minimal required information for KYC. Enable 2FA and strong passwords. Monitor for data breaches and freeze credit if exchange data is compromised.

items.task: Know what identity verification costs you, and what an unregistered venue costs you
items.why: A verified exchange keeps a permanent record tying you to your addresses. A venue with no checks may be unregistered, which carries its own legal and counterparty risk.
items.howTo: Don't assume a platform is unverified because an old guide says so: KuCoin made KYC compulsory on 15 July 2023, and in January 2025 it pleaded guilty in the US and agreed to leave that market for at least two years.

pro_tips: Layer techniques that protect different things: Tor hides your IP address, while CoinJoin or privacy coins break the transaction trail. Stacking a VPN on top of Tor doesn't add anonymity.
Privacy coins like Monero hide the amount, sender and receiver by default, which is a stronger guarantee than anything you can bolt onto Bitcoin after the fact.
Time correlation attacks can link mixed transactions - add random delays of hours or days between privacy operations to break timing analysis.
Chain analysis companies are constantly improving - stay updated on new privacy techniques and tools as the cat-and-mouse game continues.
Test your privacy setup with small amounts first - mistakes with large sums can permanently compromise your financial privacy and security.
